text: there was insufficient evidence to support a policy of routinely stopping combined oral contraceptives before major surgery. Additional- ly, there was insufficient evidence to support routine specific thromboembolic prophylaxis in women without additional risk factors. A review8 has subsequently recommended that women for whom major elective surgery was planned should continue taking the combined oral contraceptive but should receive thromboprophylaxis in the perioperative period. It has also been pointed out9,10 that for patients awaiting surgery who require contraception, a progestogen-only oral contraceptive or an injec- tion of medroxyprogesterone acetate may be suitable since nei- ther preparation increases the risk of thrombosis. 1. For a warning that women taking oral contraceptives may be at increased risk of deep-vein thrombosis from travel in- volving prolonged immobility see Cardiovascular Disease, above. Interactions Enzyme-inducing drugs can cause combined oral con- traceptives to fail by increasing their metabolism and clearance.
